budget_fy2025_memo.docx.text:
FY2025 Operating Budget - Memo to the Board

From: Office of the Chief Financial Officer. Date: March 12, 2025. Subject: proposed operating budget for fiscal year 2025, for approval at the March 20 Board meeting.

1. Summary

The proposed operating expense budget for FY2025 is $268 million, an increase of 12% over FY2024 actual operating expenses of $239 million. Capital expenditure is budgeted at $34 million, mainly for data-center capacity in Frankfurt and Virginia.

2. Operating Expenses by Function

Research and development: $112 million.

Sales and marketing: $98 million.

General and administrative: $58 million.

3. Headcount

The plan adds 220 net new employees over the year, 60% of them in research and development. Most hires are planned for the second half of the year.

4. Cost Measures

The company-wide travel budget is reduced by 10% compared to FY2024. External consulting spend is capped at $9 million. Any new spend above the approved budget for a function requires approval from the Chief Financial Officer.

5. Risks

The budget assumes revenue growth at the midpoint of guidance, about 15.5%. If growth falls below 14%, the hiring plan for the second half will be reduced by up to half.

information_security_policy.pdf.text:
Information Security Policy

Policy owner: Chief Information Security Officer. Version 5.0, effective February 1, 2025. Applies to all employees, contractors and systems of Acme Corporation.

1. Data Classification

Acme classifies information into four levels: Public, Internal, Confidential and Restricted. Customer data and employee personal data are always Restricted. Restricted data may only be stored in approved production systems and may never be copied to personal devices.

2. Passwords and Authentication

Passwords must be at least fourteen (14) characters long. Multi-factor authentication is required for every company system that supports it, including email, source control and the VPN. Passwords are not rotated on a schedule; they must be changed immediately when a compromise is suspected.

3. Devices

Company laptops must use full-disk encryption, automatic screen lock after five (5) minutes of inactivity and the managed endpoint protection agent. Lost or stolen devices must be reported to the IT service desk within four (4) hours.

4. Access Control

Access is granted on a least-privilege basis and reviewed every quarter by the system owner. Access for departing employees is revoked on their last working day.

5. Incident Reporting

Employees must report any suspected security incident to security@acme.example within one (1) hour of noticing it. The security team classifies incidents by severity and leads the response.

6. Training

All employees complete security awareness training when they join and every year after that. Employees who fail a simulated phishing test complete a short refresher course within fourteen (14) days.

7. Vendors

A vendor that will process Confidential or Restricted data must pass a security review before a contract is signed. The review is repeated every two (2) years.

8. Exceptions

Exceptions to this policy require written approval from the Chief Information Security Officer and expire after twelve (12) months.

leave_policy.docx.text:
Leave Policy

This policy describes the types of leave available to employees of Acme Corporation in addition to the paid time off described in the Employee Handbook. Effective January 1, 2025.

1. Parental Leave

A primary caregiver receives sixteen (16) weeks of fully paid parental leave. A secondary caregiver receives eight (8) weeks of fully paid parental leave. Parental leave must be taken within twelve (12) months of the birth, adoption or foster placement, and is available after three (3) months of employment.

2. Sick Leave

Employees receive ten (10) days of paid sick leave per calendar year. Sick leave does not carry over to the following year. A medical certificate is required for an absence of more than three (3) consecutive working days.

3. Bereavement Leave

Employees receive up to five (5) days of paid bereavement leave on the death of an immediate family member, and up to two (2) days for an extended family member.

4. Jury Duty

Employees called for jury duty receive full pay for up to ten (10) working days per year.

5. Sabbatical

After five (5) years of continuous employment, employees may take a paid sabbatical of four (4) weeks. A sabbatical must be requested at least three (3) months in advance and approved by the employee's manager.

6. Unpaid Leave

Unpaid leave of up to three (3) months may be granted at the company's discretion. Health insurance continues during approved unpaid leave.

Mutual Non-Disclosure Agreement

This Mutual Non-Disclosure Agreement ("NDA") is made as of October 2, 2024 between Acme Corporation ("Acme") and Northwind Logistics Inc. ("Northwind"), each a "Party", in connection with discussions about a possible business relationship (the "Purpose").

1. Confidential Information

"Confidential Information" means any non-public business, technical or financial information disclosed by one Party to the other, in any form, that is marked as confidential or that a reasonable person would understand to be confidential.

2. Exclusions

Confidential Information does not include information that the receiving Party can show: (a) is or becomes publicly available through no fault of the receiving Party; (b) was lawfully known to it before disclosure; (c) is received from a third party without a duty of confidentiality; or (d) is independently developed without use of the disclosing Party's information.

3. Obligations

The receiving Party shall use Confidential Information only for the Purpose, shall not disclose it to anyone other than its employees and advisers who need to know it for the Purpose and are bound by obligations at least as protective as this NDA, and shall not reverse engineer, decompile or disassemble any software or prototype it receives.

4. Compelled Disclosure

If the receiving Party is required by law or court order to disclose Confidential Information, it shall give the disclosing Party prompt written notice, where legally permitted, so that the disclosing Party may seek a protective order.

5. Term

This NDA remains in effect for two (2) years from the date above. The obligations of confidentiality survive for three (3) years after the NDA expires or is terminated.

6. Return or Destruction

Within fifteen (15) days of a written request, the receiving Party shall return or destroy all Confidential Information of the disclosing Party and confirm the destruction in writing, except for copies retained in automatic backup systems, which remain subject to this NDA.

7. No License or Obligation

Nothing in this NDA grants any license under any patent, copyright or other intellectual property right, and neither Party is obliged to enter into any further agreement.

8. Governing Law

This NDA is governed by the laws of the State of New York. Each Party submits to the exclusive jurisdiction of the state and federal courts located in New York County.

Order Form No. NW-2025-001

This Order Form is entered into under the Master Services Agreement dated January 15, 2024 between Acme Corporation ("Provider") and Northwind Logistics Inc., a Delaware corporation headquartered in Columbus, Ohio ("Customer"). In case of conflict, this Order Form prevails over the Master Services Agreement for the services listed below.

1. Subscription

Service: Enterprise Cloud, Professional edition.

Quantity: 250 named user seats.

Price: US$42.00 per seat per month.

Annual subscription fee: US$126,000.00.

Subscription term: twenty-four (24) months, starting February 1, 2025 and ending January 31, 2027.

2. Add-on Services

Managed Services, Standard tier: US$18,000.00 per year.

Premium Support: included at no additional charge for the subscription term.

3. Billing and Payment

Fees are invoiced annually in advance on the subscription start date and on each anniversary. Notwithstanding Section 2 of the Master Services Agreement, Customer shall pay each invoice within forty-five (45) days of the invoice date. All amounts are exclusive of taxes.

4. Data Residency

Customer data for this subscription is hosted exclusively in Provider's Frankfurt, Germany data center. Provider will not move Customer data to another region without Customer's prior written consent.

5. Premium Support

Premium Support shortens the Priority 1 response time to thirty (30) minutes, twentyfour hours a day, seven days a week. All other support response times follow the Service Level Agreement. Customer is assigned a named technical account manager.

6. Seat Changes

Customer may add seats at any time at the same per-seat price, prorated to the end of the current annual period. Seats may be reduced only at an annual renewal date, and never below 200 seats during the subscription term.

7. Renewal

This Order Form renews automatically for successive twelve (12) month periods unless either party gives written notice of non-renewal at least sixty (60) days before the end of the then-current term. Renewal pricing may increase by no more than five percent (5%) per year.

Signatures

Signed for Acme Corporation by Maria Chen, Vice President of Sales, on January 20, 2025. Signed for Northwind Logistics Inc. by Tom Becker, Chief Operating Officer, on January 22, 2025.

Acme Corporation - Quarterly Report Q1 FY2025

Quarter ended March 31, 2025. Prepared for the Board of Directors, dated April 24, 2025. All figures in United States dollars and unaudited.

Highlights

Total revenue for the first quarter of fiscal year 2025 was $128.9 million, an increase of 17.2% compared to $110.0 million in the first quarter of fiscal year 2024. Growth was led by Enterprise Cloud, which added 41 new enterprise customers in the quarter.

Revenue by Segment

Enterprise Cloud subscription revenue: $86.4 million, up 22.5% year over year.

Managed Services revenue: $32.1 million, up 9.6% year over year.

Other revenue: $10.4 million, down 1.9% year over year.

Profitability

Gross margin was 72.6%, compared to 70.9% in the same quarter last year. Operating income was $21.3 million. Operating expenses grew more slowly than revenue because hiring was concentrated in the second half of the fiscal year.

Cash

Cash and cash equivalents were $231.8 million at the end of the quarter. Operating cash flow for the quarter was $26.7 million. The share repurchase program approved in March had not started by the end of the quarter.

Customers and People

Net revenue retention for Enterprise Cloud was 118%. Headcount at the end of the quarter was 1,940 employees.

Outlook

Management reaffirms its fiscal year 2025 guidance of revenue growth between 14% and 17%. Guidance for the second quarter is revenue between $132 million and $135 million.

Statement of Work No. 1 - Data Migration

This Statement of Work ("SOW") is issued under the Master Services Agreement dated January 15, 2024 between Acme Corporation ("Provider") and Northwind Logistics Inc. ("Customer"). It describes the migration of Customer's shipment-tracking data from its legacy on-premises system to Enterprise Cloud.

1. Scope

Provider will extract, transform and load approximately 40 million shipment records and 1.2 terabytes of attached documents from Customer's legacy Oracle database into Enterprise Cloud, and will validate record counts and checksums after each load.

2. Out of Scope

Migration of archived records older than seven (7) years, changes to Customer's internal reporting tools, and end-user training are not included in this SOW.

3. Timeline

The project runs for twelve (12) weeks starting March 3, 2025. The cutover to production is planned for the weekend of May 24, 2025.

4. Fees and Milestones

The fixed fee for this SOW is US$85,000, invoiced on completion of three milestones:

Milestone 1, approved migration plan: 30% of the fee.

Milestone 2, successful test migration in the staging environment: 40% of the fee.

Milestone 3, production cutover accepted by Customer: 30% of the fee.

Travel expenses are billed separately at cost and may not exceed US$6,000 without Customer's written approval.

5. Acceptance

Customer has ten (10) business days after each milestone delivery to accept it or to describe in writing how it does not meet this SOW. A milestone not rejected within that period is deemed accepted.

6. Change Requests

Any change to scope, timeline or fees requires a written change request signed by both parties. Provider will estimate the impact of a requested change within five (5) business days.

7. Project Contacts

Provider's project manager is Lena Park. Customer's project sponsor is Tom Becker, Chief Operating Officer.

Travel and Expense Policy

Policy owner: Finance. Version 3.2, effective January 1, 2025. This policy applies to all employees of Acme Corporation who travel or incur expenses on company business.

1. Approval

All business travel must be approved in advance by the employee's manager through the travel booking tool. International travel also requires approval from a Vice President.

2. Air Travel

Employees book economy class for flights scheduled at six (6) hours or less. Business class is allowed for flights scheduled at more than six (6) hours, with the approval of a Vice President. Tickets should be booked at least fourteen (14) days before departure when possible.

3. Hotels

The nightly hotel rate, excluding taxes, may not exceed US$250. In New York, London and San Francisco the limit is US$325 per night. Employees must use the preferred hotels listed in the booking tool when one is available.

4. Meals

Employees receive a meal per diem of US$75 per full travel day, and US$40 on the days of departure and return. The per diem replaces individual meal receipts. Alcohol is not reimbursable, except during client entertainment approved in advance by a Director.

5. Ground Transportation

Employees should use public transport or taxis. Rental cars are allowed when cheaper than the alternatives or when traveling with colleagues. Use of a personal car is reimbursed at US$0.67 per mile.

6. Receipts and Submission

An itemized receipt is required for every expense of US$25 or more. Expense claims must be submitted within thirty (30) days after the trip ends. Claims submitted more than ninety (90) days after the trip are not reimbursed.

7. Non-reimbursable Expenses

The following are not reimbursed: upgrades paid for personally, airline lounge memberships, traffic and parking fines, personal entertainment, and expenses for a spouse or family member.

8. Corporate Card

Employees who travel more than four (4) times per year are issued a corporate card. Personal expenses must never be charged to it.
